aggressive_definition: Aggressive prostate cancer, with no grade, stage, metastatic, or lethal threshold specified in the abstract.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate the relative risk of total (n = 2,041) and aggressive (n = 461) prostate cancer by quintiles of baseline and 3-year serum retinol concentrations and by change in serum retinol levels from baseline to 3 years.
study_design: Prospective cohort analysis within the Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study cohort
cohort_total_n_excerpt: The authors prospectively examined prostate cancer risk and serum retinol levels, measured by using high-performance liquid chromatography, at baseline (n = 29,104) and after 3 years (n = 22,843) in the Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study cohort.
reason: The prospective cohort analysis explicitly estimated risks of both total and aggressive incident prostate cancer. The abstract does not further define aggressive disease.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Men with higher retinol concentrations at baseline were more likely to develop prostate cancer (quintile 5 vs. quintile 1 hazard ratio = 1.19, 95% confidence interval: 1.03, 1.36; P(trend) = 0.009).
estimate_classifications.reason: The HR of 1.19 is reported for prostate cancer generally. The subsequent statement that results were similar for aggressive disease does not make this overall estimate an aggressive estimate.

additional_estimates.comparison: Quintile 5 versus quintile 1 of baseline serum retinol
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: Men with higher retinol concentrations at baseline were more likely to develop prostate cancer (quintile 5 vs. quintile 1 hazard ratio = 1.19, 95% confidence interval: 1.03, 1.36; P(trend) = 0.009). The results were similar for aggressive disease.
